headline: 1Password is locked; the broker is functioning normally
summary: The alert followed a real 1Password lock at 03:36:58 Eastern on October 12. Both accounts had successful keepalive calls at 03:34:12 and 03:34:13. The broker stayed alive and keepalive correctly suppressed authenticated calls while locked.
cause: The bounded application-log parser found a latest timestamped lock event at 2026-10-12T07:36:58.720+00:00, matching keepalive state. No parser regression, stalled watchdog or broker crash was observed. Why the app locked is not established. Previous account successes are historical and do not prove authorization survives the lock.
resolution: No code change is warranted. No implementation, service installation, broker restart, keepalive replacement, permission change or additional auth wake was performed. Synthetic lock/rotation, authorization/backoff, recovery-gate and broker isolation tests passed.
verification: 44 Python tests passed across test_keepalive, test_recovery, test_op_agent, test_activation and test_agent_guidance; 37 Node tests passed across settlement, archive and recovery dispatch. Source/deployed worker and keepalive hashes match; running keepalive hash and build stamp match; bundle signature verifies. The absolute bin/op --version wrapper returned 0 with stdout/stderr discarded. Heartbeat advanced from 03:37:55 to 03:38:36; final heartbeat age was 8 seconds. Broker PID 1051, session 1051, /dev/ttys000 and keepalive PID 1055 were preserved. The exact incident title, dotfiles cwd, Pinned section, strongest advertised gpt-6-astra model and high effort were read back.
activation: Existing installed code remains running. Nothing is staged and no activation command is required. Taylor must unlock 1Password before authenticated work can resume and personally approve any native consent requested. Recovery owns any notification-click auth wake; this incident adds no retry loop.
limitations: Authenticated account calls were deliberately not attempted while 1Password was locked. Post-unlock account authorization and physical notification/Touch ID behavior were not tested. Settling this software diagnosis does not mean the app has been unlocked or accounts have been reauthorized.
docs: Reviewed src/onepassword/README.md, agent-contract.md and autofixes/AGENTS.md. Updated README.md with this verified lock incident and the distinction between historical success and current authorization. Existing agent-contract.md already covers the required boundaries, so no contract change or guidance sync was needed.
